Title: Diagnosis of test `org.apache.commons.compress.ArchiveUtilsTest.sanitizeShortensString()`

Details: 
The test `sanitizeShortensString` constructs a long string input (significantly longer than 255 characters) composed entirely of digits repeated many times. The expected output is the same string but truncated and appended with ellipsis ("...") to indicate shortening.

Looking at the method under test, `ArchiveUtils.sanitize(String)`, its JavaDoc states that the sanitized string replaces non-printable characters with '?' and also the outcome "is not longer than 255 chars." However, the actual implementation shown does not enforce any length limit on the output string.

The implementation iterates over the characters of the input string, appends valid printable characters, and replaces control or special unicode block characters with '?', but it never shortens the string or adds a trailing "..." as the test expects.

Because the function returns the fully sanitized string without shortening it to 255 chars, the test `sanitizeShortensString` fails due to mismatch: the test expects truncation plus ellipsis, but the actual output is the full-length string (or at least longer than expected).

This discrepancy occurs because the method `sanitize` implementation does not have any logic to shorten the string or append ellipsis, whereas the test expects such behavior as described in the method's JavaDoc but not implemented.

---

The best location to fix this issue would be in the method that performs the sanitation, specifically to add the logic to shorten the string and append the ellipsis if the length exceeds 255 characters.

Recommended method to fix:
org.apache.commons.compress.ArchiveUtils.sanitize(java.lang.String)
